_readme: [SHIP-GATE-1] What SUCCESS looks like, in telemetry, for every issue that ships behaviour to app/ or worker/. Written BEFORE the build goes out, not after. tool/check_ship_readiness.py --check manifest fails when an issue shipped without an entry here; --check telemetry queries PostHog and fails when the events are absent OR present-but-carrying-a-failure-value. Written on 2026-08-08 because three of four call fixes shipped the day before and did nothing: the telemetry arrived saying `presence=unknown decision=ring_unknown` on every single call and was reported as 'telemetry is flowing'. Event and property names below were read out of the emit sites in the code, not from memory — see `_verified_at` on each entry.
_schema: See the module docstring of tool/check_ship_readiness.py. Required per entry: description, two_sided, min_devices_on_build, flags, success[]. Escape hatch for a commit that ships no user-visible behaviour: "no_telemetry": "<reason>" (a reason is mandatory).

CALL-PRESENCE-3.description: No-record is also offline (owner's rule, the Arti call avatok-6e17cdc2 2026-08-09): a clean presence read MISS means the account has not checked in for at least the key TTL (>= presenceOfflineSec*6) or never - route straight to Ava with offline_by=no_record. error/timeout reads stay fail-open to ringing. Combined with minAppBuild=10528 forcing all installs onto heartbeat-capable builds, every callee is now either fresh (ring), stale<5min (ring), stale>=5min (Ava), or no-record (Ava). Server-side only.

success.note: The Arti scenario: call an account with no presence record (inactive account on a shared phone). Ava must engage without ring cycles. ring_unknown with presence_read=miss after this ships means presenceOfflineSec was set <= 0 or the deploy did not land.

CALL-PRESENCE-3._verified_at: worker/src/routes/api.ts noRecord = presenceRead === 'miss' && offlineMs > 0, offlineBy no_record, decision receptionist_offline_immediate

CALL-RING-AUDIBLE-3.description: The 'sound almost died at beep 7' after CALL-RING-AUDIBLE-2: the tone kept PLAYING (ringback_audible proved it) but the receptionist prewarm's startEngine set MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION + re-selected the communication device + opened an AEC AudioTrack on the same voice output the tone uses, 8s before Ava spoke. Fix: defer the native engine start to the ava-live gate (tone stop and mode switch become simultaneous), re-pin the user's speaker choice at the gate (a Speaker press during prewarm never reached the prewarming call - it could open on earpiece), keep mic available for the voicemail-fallback lane. Flag-gated on callRingAudibilityV1 (true in prod).

success.note: Engine opened AT/AFTER Ava's first audio. gate_open=false with deferred=false is the pre-fix bug; gate_open=false with deferred=true is legitimately the voicemail-fallback lane ONLY. Cross-check: at_ms_since_ring >= the ringback_audible phase=prewarm 2000ms sample.

CALL-PRESENCE-2.description: Owner's rule made real: a callee whose phone has not heartbeated for presenceOfflineSec (default 300s) routes the caller STRAIGHT to Ava instead of a blind ring. Before this, ring_stale was a telemetry label nothing branched on, and receptionist_offline additionally required token_count=0 - which a switched-off phone never satisfies (FCM tokens survive power-off). Also: Upstash presence reads got a 1.2s timeout + retry and an outcome (hit|miss|error|timeout) - the 11:22 unknown-while-beats-flowed was a swallowed read error. Server-side only: works on every build already in the field.

success.note: Emitted ONLY when the age arm fired with token_count > 0, so it cannot be confused with the legacy zero-token receptionist_offline. Requires a real test: call someone whose phone has been off/backgrounded-dead for >5 min. offline_by=age and offline_sec=300 on the same event corroborate.

The 2c fix: reads that fail are now VISIBLE (decision=ring_unknown_read_failed). A run of error/timeout means Upstash is unhealthy or the 1.2s deadline is too tight - the call still rings (fail-open by design), but presence routing is inert while it lasts.

CALL-PRESENCE-2._verified_at: worker/src/routes/api.ts offline test stale && (n===0 || ageMs >= presenceOfflineSec*1000), decision receptionist_offline_immediate; worker/src/lib/redis.ts redisGetJsonResult outcome; commit 20ca06ca

CALL-RING-AUDIBLE-2.description: Ringback silence mid-beeps was our own code: three leftover _ringback.stop() calls on the unreachable lane (12s device-wake timer in start(), ok:false ring-ack, re-armed timer in notePlaceResult) killed the tone ~12s in, and the 'sound waking up' was Ava's first audio 6-8s later. AVA-PREWARM-1 had fixed _onNoAnswer but left these three callers. New _goUnreachable keeps the tone playing until the ava-live gate (Ava's first real audio) or handoff failure. NOT the audio-owner race and NOT prewarm focus - route was speaker throughout; verified against AvaVoiceAudioPlugin.kt focus types.

success.note: Sampled at prewarm start and +2s; playing=true at the 2s sample with position_ms CHANGED vs the 0ms sample is the pass. playing=false or identical position_ms is the pre-fix silence. Flag callRingAudibilityV1 must be ON and the caller's phone on the new build; flag off = byte-equivalent old behavior.

CALL-RTK-2.description: Worker half of the RealtimeKit migration (Specs/CALL-REALTIMEKIT-MIGRATION.md): POST /api/callrtk/:room/join mints a RealtimeKit participant token after verifying CallRoom admission; meeting id is first-writer-wins on the DO with a 6h lazy expiry. Ships dark: callRealtimeKitV1 and groupRealtimeKitV1 default false, and the route 503s rtk_unavailable until CF_RTK_ORG_ID/CF_RTK_API_KEY secrets are set and the three avatok_* presets exist in the RealtimeKit dashboard.

success.note: Only meaningful once a flag is flipped AND secrets/presets exist; while dark, every request emits call_rtk_blocked with reason=flag_off, which is correct behaviour, not failure. A join that returns without a meeting_id means the CF API response envelope changed shape (the route accepts both result.* and data.* — see call_rtk.ts) and the client got a token to nowhere.

CALL-RTK-3.description: Client half of the RealtimeKit migration: realtimekit_provider.dart (realtimekit_core 0.1.6) behind the rtc_provider seam, rtk-start/rtk-abort fork in call_session.dart with abort-to-legacy fallback, group early-branch behind groupRealtimeKitV1. Two-sided: both phones must be on a build that understands rtk-start, or the peer treats it as an unknown frame and the decider self-aborts to P2P at callRtkJoinDeadlineSec - which looks like 'RTK never activates' rather than an error. The connected-signal wiring landed in [CALL-RTK-4]: the joined session's events now drive the call lifecycle (ring timeout, connect watchdogs, ringback, phase) instead of leaving the call stuck in 'connecting', so RTK calls log real durations via _connectedAtMs.

success.note: outcome=joined is the pass value. A run of timeouts with the flag on means secrets/presets are wrong server-side (check call_rtk_blocked/call_rtk_error on the same window) or the SDK API-name guesses in realtimekit_provider.dart did not survive CI - either way the calls themselves still work via the rtk-abort fallback, so users won't complain; only this event says the feature is inert.
Spec §5 Phase 1/2 assertion. Emitted in realtimekit_provider.dart after joinRoom succeeds, for both 1:1 and group.

THE WHATSAPP TEST (spec §5 Phase 2): outcome=survived on a deliberate WiFi->cellular switch mid-call, on two phones both on the new build. This event only exists when a network transition actually happened - it needs the deliberate two-phone test, it will not accumulate on its own. Do not describe [CALL-RTK-3] as shipped until this has been read with outcome=survived.

CALL-RTK-4.description: Wire the joined RealtimeKit session's normalized events into the call lifecycle. Before this, _startRtkMedia joined a meeting and then told the call system nothing: _connected stayed false, so the 45s connect watchdog ended a live RTK call with 'network-error', the 22s ring timeout handed a conversation in progress to the receptionist, the ringback never stopped, and every RTK call logged duration 0 (CALL-LOG-TIME-1 keys on _connectedAtMs). The pc-stats media watchdog and first-audio probe are deliberately NOT started on this path - there is no _pc - so provider socket-state monitoring (call_network_handover) plus the error-before-connect fallback are the only health signals.

success.note: The whole point of the issue: an RTK call that reaches the 'connected' phase. Its ABSENCE while call_rtk_active is present is the exact pre-fix bug (joined, never connected). via=remote_track is the preferred signal (remote media, mirrors pc.onTrack); via=remote_join is the roster backstop for a peer that was already publishing before we joined.

media_path='rtk' only exists on this event because CALL-RTK-4 reports first audio from the SDK's remote-audio callback (the pc-stats probe cannot run - there is no _pc, so bytes_received stays at its -1 unknown sentinel and must NOT be read as a byte count). Its ABSENCE while call_rtk_active is present is the pre-fix bug: joined a meeting, never connected.

CALL-AUDIO-OWNER-1.description: CallAudioController is the single owner of call route/mode/speaker. The fix IS the equality: the route we asked for is the route the device confirmed. Before it, _bootMedia's hardcoded selectRoute(earpiece) raced the user's own Speaker press and won, which is the loud-quiet-loud outgoing tone.

success.note: Both props are the same enum rendered with .name (CallAudioRoute), so string equality is exact. The error path stamps confirmed_route='error', which fails this on purpose. A genuine device override (a Bluetooth headset taking the route) is the ONLY legitimate mismatch; if it shows up, express it with a `where` filter on `backend`, do not lower min_pass_rate.

CALL-RING-FASTPATH-1.description: Parallelise the pre-ring reads so the WS ring leaves the Worker in under a second. `ms` is cumulative from the caller pressing dial (t0 is taken before auth), so the ws_ring stage IS the answer to 'how long until their phone could ring'.

success.note: 0.9, not 1.0: a cold isolate, a D1 read that misses, or a caller on a bad mobile link genuinely blows a 1.5s budget occasionally. The regression this must catch is the MEDIAN moving back over the budget, not one slow call. If this drops below 0.9, read the other stages (admit/config/participants) in the same event to see which await came back onto the critical path.

CALL-RING-FASTPATH-1._verified_at: worker/src/routes/api.ts:292 (trackUserContact ... 'call_ring_path_ms', {stage, ms, fastpath}) and api.ts:1153 markRingStage("ws_ring")

CALL-PRESENCE-1.description: Real device heartbeat plus presence-first call routing: /api/call reads a presence record BEFORE its Durable Object round-trips, so an offline callee goes straight to Ava instead of making the caller wait ~28s. THE HEARTBEAT LIVES IN THE APP, so the callee's phone must be on the new build too - this is why two_sided is true.

success.note: PresenceState is fresh|stale|unknown (worker/src/lib/presence.ts:55). `unknown` means no record, no Upstash credentials, a read error, or a client too old to beat - i.e. the heartbeat is not arriving and the whole feature is inert. On 2026-08-08 this was `unknown` on EVERY call and was reported as shipped.

`ring_unknown` is the fall-through that rings exactly as before presence existed. Any of ring_fresh / ring_stale / ring_offline_ineligible / receptionist_offline means presence actually decided something.

CALL-PRESENCE-1._verified_at: worker/src/routes/api.ts:538-561 (props {presence, presence_age_ms, decision, routing_reason, ...}, emitted for BOTH parties via trackUser) and api.ts:620-629 (decision values)

CALL-4RINGS-1.description: Ava takes over after four REAL ring cycles instead of at a wall-clock alarm. The callee's PushService.reportRinging repeats with a monotonic ringIndex while the phone is genuinely ringing, and the CallRoom counts the AUDIBLE ones. Two-sided: the repeating receipts come from the callee's app, so a callee on an old build produces zero of them and the server silently falls back to the 20s deadline.

success.note: Filtered to counted=true on purpose. counted=false is LEGITIMATE and common - the audibility echo re-POSTs the same ringIndex, and a silent/DND phone is relayed and recorded but deliberately excluded from the count (call_room.ts:2100-2131). The failure mode this catches is that NO cycle is ever counted, i.e. ring_count stays 0.

The three trigger values are rings_completed | backstop_timeout | ring_timeout_no_receipts (call_room.ts:1306). `ring_timeout_no_receipts` means the deadline fired with ZERO ring receipts - the exact string sitting in prod on 2026-08-08 alongside ring_count=0 while the fix was being reported as shipped.

CALL-4RINGS-1._verified_at: worker/src/do/call_room.ts:2167 (trackRingEvent 'call_ring_cycle', {ring_index, counted, ring_count, audible, derived, ...}) and call_room.ts:1373 (trackRingEvent 'call_receptionist_trigger', {trigger, ring_count, ...})

CALL-LOG-TIME-1.description: Call history shows date, time AND duration on both surfaces (AvaTalk Calls tab, AvaDialer Call logs) from one shared formatter. The call-log row is written at call START, so duration/outcome did not exist at all; CallSession now closes the row out at teardown. Client-only.

success.note: op=finish is the NEW second write, emitted only by CallLogStore.finish (call_log_store.dart). Its absence means the row is still being written once, at call start, with no duration - i.e. the whole fix is inert. An empty outcome would mean _finishCallLog ran without a phase to map.

The point of the issue. A connected call reporting duration_sec=0 means _connectedAtMs was never stamped (onTrack did not fire, or the SFU lane bypassed it) and the UI will silently fall back to date+time with no duration.

CALL-DEADAIR-1.description: Kill the silence between 'the call says connected' and the first audible byte. Prod avatok-17f145b5 (2026-08-07, build 10523) measured ~14s from call_started to the first call_media_health sample carrying real audio, on a link with 5-6ms jitter and ~0% loss on BOTH sides - our setup latency, not the network. Two changes: the setup prologue (renderer init, ICE fetch, network-class probe) now runs concurrently with getUserMedia instead of ahead of it, and the SFU transport polls for the peer's seat concurrently with its own publish instead of strictly after it. The new call_first_audio_ms event is the instrument: it measures at 200ms resolution, where the only pre-existing inbound-byte sampler is a 5s periodic armed at connect and therefore quantises every answer to +/-5s.

success.note: THE number this issue is judged on. ms_from_connected is measured from _connectedAtMs (first remote track, i.e. the moment the UI says 'connected') to the first inbound-rtp audio byte. 0.8 rather than 1.0 because a genuinely bad mobile link can blow a 1s DTLS/RTP budget on its own; the regression to catch is the MEDIAN going back over 1s, not one slow call. Do NOT read this event's average across all outcomes - filter to outcome=audio, since a timeout row carries a 25s ms_from_connected by construction.
success.two_sided_note: The peer-seat poll overlap only helps when BOTH phones run the new ladder, so count distinct persons on the newest $app_build before believing an improvement.

success.note: outcome is audio|timeout|ended (call_session.dart _reportFirstAudio). 'timeout' means 25s passed on a connected call with zero inbound audio bytes - the dead-air failure itself. 'ended' means the call was hung up before any audio arrived, which is what the tester did on avatok-17f145b5. Either value dominating means the fix did nothing.

Guards the INSTRUMENT, not the fix. An empty stages_seen means _setupT0 was never anchored or _stage() never ran, so every stage_* property is missing and the per-rung breakdown - the only thing that says WHICH await ate the time - is silently absent. Read stage_sfu_join / stage_sfu_publish / stage_sfu_peer_seat / stage_sfu_pull_audio / stage_first_remote_track / stage_first_audio_bytes to attribute a regression.

AVA-VM-FALLBACK-1.description: An Ava timeout must never end the call. Prod avatok-946b6090 (2026-08-07 20:52 IST, build 10523): the receptionist session opened, produced no audio, hit ava_live_timeout after 4.5s, retried, and the call was ENDED at 20:53:19.9 with reason=ava-live-timeout while the owner was trying to leave a voicemail. He never spoke and nothing was recorded. The session is now DEGRADED in place instead: one vm_fallback control frame on the already-open socket makes ReceptionRoomCf abandon the conversational engine and run its existing deterministic voicemail flow (cached greeting -> beep -> record), so the message is stored and delivered by the same finalize() as every other receptionist voicemail. A second /api/receptionist/start was deliberately NOT used - it is refused by the KV reattach lock, the CallRoom DO ownership claim and the control-plane authority, all of which correctly exist to stop two Avas on one call.

success.note: stored comes from the SERVER's vm_result frame, not the app's guess: the DO reports false when the fallback recording carried under 0.5s of caller audio or never crossed an audible peak, which is the deliberate empty-recording guard (a card with turns:0 and no Play button is what confused the owner in July). 0.5 rather than 1.0 because a caller who says nothing at all is a legitimate, correctly-rejected outcome - the failure to catch is stored=false EVERY time, which would mean the recorder is not capturing.
success.server_note: Server mirror with the same numbers: ava_vm_fallback_result {stored, recorded_ms, caller_rec_bytes, caller_peak} on the OWNER's timeline.

success.note: A stored voicemail must contain audio. recorded_ms is computed on the server from callerRecBytes at 48000 bytes/sec (24kHz mono PCM16), so it is measured caller audio, not wall clock. stored=true with recorded_ms under the 500ms floor would mean the empty-recording guard is not being applied.

THE REGRESSION TEST, and the most important assertion here. `ava-live-timeout` is the exact terminal reason from the incident. After this change no call may end with it: the only remaining terminal reason on this path is `ava-vm-fallback-timeout`, which means the deterministic greeting AND the locally-generated beep both failed to arrive - a dead socket, not a slow model. Seeing ava-live-timeout again means the flag is off, the client is on an old build, or requestVoicemailFallback returned false.

CALL-HONEST-FAIL-1.description: Tell the caller WHY the call stopped. The terminal reason was always known (21 distinct call_ended.reason values in 7 days of prod) and never rendered; ten attempts on 2026-08-07 all looked identical to the user. ONE table (app/lib/core/ui/call_failure_copy.dart) maps reason/scenario/outcome -> a sentence, shown on the call screen and on both call-log lists. Success is NOT 'the event fired' — it is that the event carries a REAL message_key, because an unmapped ending deliberately emits nothing at all.

success.note: A failed call that told the user nothing emits NO event, so absence here is the failure mode this issue exists to fix: it means the terminal reason fell outside the table and the caller was left guessing again. Cross-check against call_ended in the same window — every call_ended whose reason is in the explained set should have a paired call_failure_shown on the same call_id.
Guards the taxonomy: a third surface added later must be added here deliberately, not discovered in a dashboard.

CALLREC-PEERNAME-1.description: Recording Inbox card said 'Call with Unknown' for a call whose peer_uid was present the whole time (owner report 2026-08-09, call avatok-85dc200b). The worker now backfills peer_name AND peer_avatar from publicIdentityFor(peer_uid) in finalizeRecording when the client sent none; the client's own value still wins (group-escalation labels). Server-side only, so shipped clients get named cards on their NEXT recording with no app update.

success.note: Emitted by the server finalize. 'server' means the backfill did the work; a steady stream of 'none' with a non-empty peer_uid means publicIdentityFor found no profile row and the card will still read Unknown - which is the failure this issue exists to fix.
